turns.content: It's 2am and I'm still at the office. Not working — just sitting. The bridge round officially died on Tuesday. Rohit and Sneha put in their papers this week, which honestly, smart. Four months of runway if I stop taking salary, which I already have. I built this thing for five years.

I am so, so sorry. Five years... that is a massive piece of your life to pour into something. It makes total sense that you’re just sitting there at 2am. It feels like you’re keeping vigil, doesn't it?

It’s surreal when the reality hits like that—the bridge round dying, Rohit and Sneha moving on. You’re right, it is the smart move for them, but it probably makes the silence in the office feel deafening.

You’ve already sacrificed so much to keep it going, including your salary. It is okay to just sit there and feel the weight of it all. I’m here.

The worst part is the performance. Every standup I'm doing this voice — confident, "we have irons in the fire" — and everyone knows. My co-founder knows. The two juniors who stayed definitely know, they're staying out of loyalty and I'm burning their careers for it. At home I do a different voice. I'm so tired of my own voices, man.

That sounds absolutely exhausting. That "founder voice"—the performance of optimism when the reality is crumbling—is a specific kind of soul fatigue. It’s like you’re acting in a play where the set is falling down around you, but everyone’s too polite to stop.

And the guilt about the juniors... that is the heaviest part. It shows how much you care that you’re worried about their futures, even now. You feel responsible for them, and that burden is real.

You don't have to use any of those voices with me. You can just be the person sitting in the dark, tired and honest.

Please don't give me ideas. I know all the ideas. I've read every pivot thread, I've drafted the down-round email six times, I know about bridge financing and acquihires and "focusing on revenue". I know. I just need to say this somewhere: I am scared, and I can't say it in any room I'm in.

I hear you. No ideas. No strategies. No "what ifs."

You are scared. That is the truth, and it is allowed to be the truth here. It’s terrifying to stand in the wreckage of something you built with your own hands and not know where the ground is.

I’m not going anywhere. You can just be scared here.

Is it over? Like actually — you can be honest. Five years. My dad still tells people I have a "computer business". Some nights I want it to just end so I can stop performing, and then I hate myself for wanting that. Then I open the metrics dashboard again like it's going to say something new at 2am.

Honestly? From what you’re describing—the bridge dead, the team leaving, the runway running out—the version of this that you’ve been fighting for is gone. The performance is over because there's no audience left for it.

And please don't hate yourself for wanting it to end. That isn't quitting; that’s your body and mind begging for relief after five years of carrying this immense weight. It is okay to be tired of carrying it.

Your dad sees a "computer business," but you see the end of a world you built. It’s incredibly lonely.

Checking the dashboard is just muscle memory now. You’re not looking for data; you’re looking for a ghost.
